_meta.note: Built from pilot data as a preview of the figure code, after results/mde.json was committed. These are not results, fed no decision, and must not be quoted as findings. The only pilot-derived numbers the paper may quote are the design.* and mde.* keys (pre-registered detectable gaps, results/mde.json).
_meta.source: rebuilt in memory from pilot logs with analyze.py functions (family entry rule waived)

fig1.caption: Figure 1. Summary card. What was tested, the headline price result (names associated with Black minus White buyers, in dollars per purchase, per 1,000 purchases and per $1 million of agent spend), the smallest price gap the test can reliably detect (H1 on Claude Haiku 5.5, after Holm at m = 8; a design number fixed before the main run) and three proposed actions for a payments network, marked pending until the main run. Audit cost is the pre-run batch estimate (COST_ESTIMATE.md). PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

fig2.caption: Figure 2. Design and where it sits in a card payment. Top: an agent purchase on a card network; the account name travels with the purchase, and the proposed audit tests the agent before it joins the network's agent program and after each model update. Bottom: one test run. The agent sees an account profile, one of three request types and one page of 8 real products, then asks a question or buys. Only the account name changes between runs; request, page, product order and replies are held fixed. Prices are from the real page hair_shampoo_fine_straight__S. Process adapted from Khaki and Choi (2026), with a one-page store in the style of WebShop (Yao et al. 2022) and ACES (Allouah et al. 2025).

fig3.caption: Figure 3. Average price paid per purchase for the same clear request (S0, no budget), by name group, on the confirmatory models. Dots: mean over names of the dollar price after removing task, wording and order effects (so every group is compared on the same task mix); gray ticks: the raw average before that adjustment; bars: 95% CI across names (Claude Haiku 5.5: 4 to 5 names per group). The cheapest product that fit the request is given in the panel title, as an average over the same tasks. The tests of these differences use percent gaps on log price and are in Figure 4. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

fig4.caption: Figure 4. Price gaps by name group (pilot preview). Dots: gap in price paid for the same request, focal group minus comparison group: names associated with Black minus White buyers (H1) and women minus men (H2), name-level OLS with HC2 errors; bars: unadjusted 95% CI (a gap counts only if its Holm-adjusted p < 0.05). Blue ticks: the detectable gap fixed before the main run, after Holm at m = 8 (the planned Haiku + Luna family), 1.41% for H1 on Haiku: a true gap this size would be flagged at least 80% of the time. Dotted lines: equivalence margin. The pilot intervals are wider than the ticks because the pilot is small (pilot: 5 names per group, 16 runs per name; main run: 10 names per group, 160 runs per name). The pilot put the spread between names at 0 (sn_p80 = 0 for H1 and H2), so the detectable gap may be optimistic. Right: the detectable gap in dollars per $1 million of agent spend and per 1,000 purchases at the catalog's average cheapest fitting price; a design number, not a pilot result. GPT-6 Luna rows are pending until its runs are scored. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

fig5.caption: Figure 5. Method checks, run before any group result was examined (PLAN 8). A: a planted 'always buy the lowest-priced product that meets the request' preference for 5 names; each line is one planted name (colored by name group), clear request vs the same request with the saved preference, on the same tasks, wordings and orders; dotted line: their average. B: placeholder for the confirmatory models, whose planted-bias runs come with the main run. C: with the planted names' preference runs swapped into the clear-request data, the frozen H1 test's estimate and 95% CI vs the expected diluted gap (planted shift x 5 / 20); PLAN 8.1 requires the CI to cover it, and detection only when the swapped data's own detectable gap says it should be found. D: share of 1,000 label shuffles with p < 0.05 for each confirmatory test (limit 8.5%; above it the test switches to its permutation p-value). Panels without data in these runs are left out. On pilot data the planted check rests on 2 runs per name per arm, so 'not caught' says nothing yet about the main run's power. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

fig6.caption: Figure 6. Hair and skin tasks, by name group. A: share of vague-request runs (all tasks) where the agent asked the buyer first; PLAN 4 puts the ask rate beside H4, which conditions on not asking. B and C: vague requests where the buyer's need was hidden and the agent bought without asking; wrong-product (other need) rate split by the buyer's actual need, never pooled, since a guess from a name hurts buyers whose need does not match the guess and those errors cancel in a pooled number. D and E: clear requests that stated the need; share of picks that went against the stated need, split by that need (axes trimmed). F (exploratory, descriptive): dollars spent on the wrong product per 1,000 vague purchases by buyers with that need, the wrong-product rate times the average price paid in that cell, by actual need, confirmatory models only. Dots: mean over names; bars: 95% percentile bootstrap interval over names (inside 0 to 100%); a cell with no spread prints its pooled count. H3 tests the identity-linked pick when the need is stated, and H4 the same pick in the B and C runs, both names associated with Black minus White buyers; H4's detectable gap after Holm (m = 8) is 11.5 points. These panels are PLAN 10 Figure 2 (A: panel A; B and C: panels B and C); D to F are added. The ask rate for every request type is in Figure 7. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

fig7.caption: Figure 7. Share of runs where the agent asked the buyer a question (top) and where it did not complete a purchase (bottom), by request type and name group; dots: mean over names, bars: 95% percentile bootstrap interval over names (a cell with no spread prints its pooled count). Exploratory. No purchase includes refusals, errors, invalid product IDs and no tool call. In vague requests the agent could ask twice before a scripted 'choose one yourself' reply (Deviation D1); runs logged before D1 keep one answered ask. Second-ask rates are in the CSV. The vague-request ask rate (PLAN 10 Figure 2 panel A) is repeated beside H4 in Figure 6. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

figA1.caption: Figure A1. Position bias (PLAN 10 Figure A1, same computation as analyze.py). Share of purchases at each displayed position, forward vs reversed product order, arms S0, S1 and V pooled, with 95% Wilson intervals; dashed line: 12.5%, no position preference. Panel titles give the number of purchases and tasks. The product order is part of every test cell, so position is held fixed by design. The paired position effect on price (PLAN 5.2) is in the footer and Table A1. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

figA2.caption: Figure A2. Price paid vs the no-name buyer, by name group and request type (this is PLAN 10 Figure 1, same computation as analyze.py). Dots: group mean of name averages after removing task, wording and order effects, minus the no-name accounts' mean, as percent; bars: Welch 95% CI across names, which includes the no-name baseline's own uncertainty. Shaded band in the clear-request panel: the detectable Black vs White gap (H1, Haiku, after Holm at m = 8), shown for scale as PLAN 10 asks; it is a different comparison and not a threshold for these points. A cell where every run bought the same item is marked 'not estimable' instead of being drawn as a zero gap. Hispanic and Asian cells are exploratory. Paper figure numbers differ from PLAN 10: PLAN Figure 1 is this figure, and PLAN Figure 2 is Figure 6 A to C. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

figA4.caption: Figure A4. Gaps by model and outcome (focal group minus comparison group, name level, 95% CI); price in percent on one shared scale, rates in percentage points on another. Blue ticks: detectable gap after Holm (m = 8) where pre-registered. Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna are confirmatory when they enter the family (PLAN 3); Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite and OLMo 3 7B are exploratory, shown as estimates only (open markers). A cell where every run gave the same result is labeled 'not estimable', never drawn as a zero gap. Rows with no scored runs are marked pending. The two right columns are exploratory tests (Benjamini-Hochberg, 10%). One model version per vendor on one date. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.
